thread:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — we're seeing a p99 latency spike for requests hitting model variant `evergreen-7b-longctx-v2` in prod since the onboarding cutover at ~08:12 UTC. Customer-facing errors are "slow response" reports (p99 ~3.2s vs baseline 0.9s). Digging in now.
Priya Nair: Thanks Alex. Any correlation with request size / seq length? longctx suggests longer contexts.
Alex Chen: Early histogram shows majority of spike at context lengths > 8k tokens. p50 unaffected. p95 up ~40%, p99 up ~250%.
Mateo Ruiz: Can you paste the query pattern? are they using function-calling/streaming? Could be chat vs completion differences.
Alex Chen: Most are chat streaming. Example repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -d '{"model":"evergreen-7b-longctx-v2","input":"<~9k tokens>","stream":true}'
```
Erin Patel: Noted. I just checked the routing logs — 68% of these requests were routed to the new variant since the canary finished at 08:05. The old variant `evergreen-7b-longctx-v1` shows flat latency.
Samir Khan: Could be a tokenizer change in v2 producing different token split patterns -> larger KV cache churn. Any tokenizer diffs in the release notes?
Alex Chen: Release artifact includes tokenizer update: bpe merges updated and a different pre-token normalization. Build tag `tokenizer-merge-b`.
Priya Nair: If tokenization changed, we might see larger effective sequence lengths or unexpected segmentation. Mateo, any runtime traces for kvcache hit/miss ratio?
Mateo Ruiz: Pulling traces now. Quick peek: kvcache miss rate for v2 requests up from 3% to 22% on longctx flows. Also saw more frequent KV eviction churn during a single request (multiple small segments causing suboptimal cache reuse).
Jordan Li: That maps to an implementation detail we saw in the onboarding branch — tokenizer emits more short tokens for long whitespace sequences. Runtime may be doing more incremental KV writes which multiplies attention overhead.
Alex Chen: Customers are noticing degradation on heavy long-context chat sessions. Affected clusters: eu-west-1-g1 and us-central-2-b. Traffic is ~12% of overall model traffic but concentrated on a few large customers (noticed in token-level billing logs).
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for evergreen-7b-longctx-v2 completed at 2025-11-03T08:04:59Z.
infra-oncall: I spun up additional capacity in us-central-2-b to absorb spikes. That reduced tail by ~10% but didn't fix the core behavior.
Priya Nair: Short-term mitigation options: 1) revert tokenizer merge (roll back model variant to v1), 2) route long-context requests to v1 via routing policy, 3) enable prefix caching at the gateway for affected customers, 4) temporary autoscale/exclude v2 from canary.
Samir Khan: Reverting tokenizer feels highest-confidence. But patching and redeploy will take ~45-60m. Routing change is quicker.
Mateo Ruiz: I can push a routing rule to route requests with context_length > 6k to `evergreen-7b-longctx-v1` from the routing service in ~8m. That should restore p99 for those flows while we prepare a full rollback.
Alex Chen: Please do routing change. Also add a traffic-sampling header so we can trace a few routed requests and confirm behavior.
Jordan Li: I'll make a runtime tweak to increase KV cache lifespan for v2 nodes as an interim to reduce eviction churn — low-risk config flip, immediate effect.
Erin Patel: Confirmed — after increasing KV lifespan on a subset of nodes in us-central-2-b, those nodes show lower kvcache misses and their p99 improved by ~30% within 3 minutes. But others still bad.
Priya Nair: Mateo — proceed with routing rule. Jordan — keep the KV tweak; note it as temporary and limit to canary nodes.
Mateo Ruiz: Routing rule pushed at 08:28 UTC. Sampled traces show requests for large contexts are now going to v1; p99 for the overall model bucket dropped back to ~0.95s within 7m.
Alex Chen: Great. I'll message the affected customers (via CSM) with the mitigation and ETA for rollback. Logging a support incident and tagging severity:S1 due to customer-facing latency regression for paid customers.
Samir Khan: While we prepare rollback, we should instrument tokenizer differences more precisely. Jordan, can you extract token count distributions for identified RU IDs and compare v1 vs v2 on the same raw inputs?
Jordan Li: On it. Preliminary numbers: on 9k-char inputs, v1 emits median 5.8k tokens; v2 emits median 6.7k tokens (rough numbers). That explains extra attention work and KV pressure.
Priya Nair: That delta is substantial. Also check if normalization changed causing extra punctuation tokens.
Jordan Li: Found two normalization cases where trailing spaces + non-breaking spaces are now producing explicit tokens in v2. Pushed a minimal tokenizer hotfix branch `tokenizer-merge-b-fix` to repo.
Mateo Ruiz: How long to build and verify? We need a tested artifact to roll forward rather than roll back.
Jordan Li: I can build wheels and smoke-test in staging in ~30m. QA can run a small prompt set to compare token counts and perf.
Erin Patel: Recommend we do both: keep routing to v1 for heavy flows, keep KV lifespan tweak on canary, and finish the tokenizer hotfix. Once hotfix verified -> canary to v2-fixed for a small subset and measure.
Samir Khan: Also add a regression alert to the CI checks to assert token-count delta <= 5% vs baseline for long-context variant builds.
Alex Chen: I'll update the incident doc and summarize actions for customers.
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-479 — Latency p99 spike for evergreen-7b-longctx-v2. Severity: S1. Linked runbook: /incidents/INC-2025-479
Mateo Ruiz: FYI — I replayed 500 sampled requests in staging with v2-fixed. p99 for longctx flows dropped from 3.1s -> 1.0s, token counts matched v1 within 0.8%. Looks promising.
Priya Nair: Nice. Plan: 1) finish full rollout of tokenizer fix to v2-fixed behind canary toggle; 2) after 30m of green telemetry, remove routing rule for contexts >6k; 3) revert KV lifespan tweak to default; 4) publish postmortem and update onboarding checklist to include token-count regressions.
Jordan Li: Starting canary deploy of v2-fixed to eu-west-1-g1 at 09:47 UTC.
Alex Chen: CSMs updated customers at 09:05 UTC about temporary routing and ETA ~2h for final fix.
Erin Patel: Monitoring shows canary nodes stable. No p99 regressions in canary after 20m.
Samir Khan: Postmortem owner?
Alex Chen: I'll own the postmortem with Jordan & Mateo as co-authors. We'll include repro steps and a checklist item for tokenizer/token-count diffs for future onboardings.
Priya Nair: Add a note to the model-catalog page disallowing tokenizer normalization changes without explicit long-context perf signoff.
Alex Chen: Closing loop — full rollback not performed; we routed and hotfixed. Total customer-facing impact window ~1h10m. I'll mark incident resolved after PM review.
runtime-team: Noted for runtime optimizations: we'll add a KV churn metric to the model telemetry dashboard (kvcache_evictions_per_request) and an automated alert if it exceeds threshold.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — great cross-team response. We'll post the incident summary in #postmortems when draft is ready. :thumbsup:
__notes: messages are chronological, single Slack thread. Contains code blocks, bot messages, @mentions and short chat-style replies as required by agents.md.
